summary.name: Nirvati
summary.one_liner: Nirvati is a free, open source personal cloud OS that lets you self-host data and apps at home, with a built-in app store of one-click installs.
use_cases: host private cloud storage at home
replace Google Drive or Dropbox with self-hosted storage
run self-hosted AI chat models locally
run a homelab on a Raspberry Pi or mini PC
summary.what_it_does: Nirvati OS is presented as a private personal cloud that runs on a mini PC, Raspberry Pi, homelab, VM, RockPro or NUC, with no specialized hardware required. It includes a web interface and app store from which popular self-hosted apps can be installed with one click. The listed apps include Nextcloud, Immich, PhotoPrism, Ollama, Open WebUI, Flowise AI and many others. The page says it is accessible from anywhere and avoids registration and privacy leaks. The awesome-selfhosted listing describes the project as Rust and Kubernetes (K8S) based, licensed AGPL-3.0.
notable: One-click app store with a large catalog of self-hosted apps
Runs on ordinary hardware such as Raspberry Pi, mini PCs and VMs
Free and open source under AGPL-3.0 (per awesome-selfhosted listing)
Built with Rust and Kubernetes according to the listing
caveats: Page text is mostly marketing; specific setup requirements and feature details are not described
Access from outside the home network is claimed but the method is not explained
